# Marginal Value of Speed — Phase 1 Results

**Generated by:** `sim/run.py` (synthetic routes, no external data)
**Spec:** `SIM-PRD.md`
**Thresholds:** fixed in advance — strong < 5 min, weak > 10 min on the 110→120 step for journeys of 3h+

---

## Verdict

**Time thesis: THESIS WEAK.** Median 110→120 benefit across 8 journeys of 3h+ is **14.7 minutes** (range 1.5 to 18.8).

**Median pass-through ratio: 1.00.** Of the driving time removed on speed-elastic segments, this is the fraction that reaches the destination.

Pass-through above 0.8 triggers the SIM-PRD section 8.1 supporting criterion: the "gains evaporate downstream" framing is not supportable and must come out of PCS.md on accuracy grounds, independent of the product decision.

## Risk-adjusted trade

Minutes bought per 100% increase in fatal-crash risk, measured against a fixed 100 km/h baseline at exponent 4. Theory predicts this falls with roughly the fifth power of speed.

| A: long motorway, free flowing | 40.1 | 31.8 | 25.5 |

## Mechanism behaviour

Pass-through by mechanism, on the 110→120 step. This is the Claim A test: below 1.0 means upstream gains are absorbed, at 1.0 they pass through untouched, above 1.0 they are amplified.

| Route | Mechanism | Pass-through | Reading |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A: long motorway, free flowing | none | 1.00 | passes gains through |
| B: motorway + urban bottleneck | M2 | 1.24 | amplifies gains |
| C: Brussels-Strasbourg (PCS 30) | M1 | 0.92 | partially absorbs |
| C2: Brussels-Strasbourg, queue variant | M2 | 1.11 | amplifies gains |
| D: cross-border, timed crossing | M3 | 0.48 | absorbs most gains |
| E: mixed motorway and secondary | none | 1.00 | passes gains through |
| F: rush-hour city arrival | M4 | 1.48 | amplifies gains |
| G: secondary-road dominated | none | 1.00 | passes gains through |
| H: motorway with roadworks | M1 | 1.00 | passes gains through |
| I: single-carriageway mixed stream | M5 | 0.64 | partially absorbs |
